entry.evidence: The chemical composition of groundwater, including SF6 concentration, was investigated to clarify the mechanism of groundwater discharge around Sanninudai

sequences.source_document: Published paper (PDF) with publisher XML text

steps.action: Pose the question of how groundwater discharges at the Sanninudai springs on the southeast coast of Yonaguni Island.
steps.quote: to clarify the mechanism of groundwater discharge around Sanninudai on the southeast coast of [...]

steps.action: Take from earlier surveys that all terrestrial water on the island carries seawater or sea salt and is enriched in limestone-derived Ca and HCO3.
steps.quote: Agata (1995) found that all terrestrial water, including surface, spring, and well water, was contaminated with seawater or contained sea salt

steps.action: Take the published interpretation that the springs are eastern outlets of the Barumi groundwater basin.
steps.quote: Kurokawa et al. (1979) recognized the springs as eastern outlets of Barumi Basin groundwater

steps.action: Design the study around adding SF6 as a groundwater age tracer, not used before on the island, to the major-ion and water-isotope analyses.
steps.quote: the concentration of sulfur hexafluoride (SF6), which has not been used in previous studies, was measured in groundwater

steps.action: Sample five springs and one mountain river (as meteoric reference) on three dates in 2019; one spring dried up in October.
steps.quote: Water was sampled from the springs and river on three occasions; 25 April, 18 June, and 27 October 2019

steps.action: Measure temperature, pH, alkalinity, anions, cations, trace elements, SF6 (purge-and-trap GC-ECD) and water isotopes (laser absorption spectroscopy).
steps.quote: SF6 was extracted using the purge-and-trap method and measured with a gas chromatograph equipped with an electron capture detector

steps.action: Compute the expected composition of seawater diluted by solute-free precipitation (dilution line) and a seawater to average-groundwater mixing line for isotopes.
steps.quote: a possible mixing line between surface seawater (Turekian, 1968) and water free from any dissolved components, representing hypothesized precipitation

steps.action: Compare each solute against the dilution line together with the 1979 and 1995 data, attributing departures to cation exchange, limestone dissolution, silicate leaching and fertilizer.
steps.quote: the components that cannot be explained by dilution of seawater alone are considered to have a surrounding solid phase as a source

steps.action: Regress isotope ratios against Cl through seawater to estimate the freshwater end-member (Cl = 0 intercept) and a mixture of about 5% seawater.
steps.quote: The spring water can be explained by a mixture of about 5% seawater and fresh water with these edge components

steps.action: Compare spring isotope data with the summer and winter local meteoric water lines and find no seasonal signal, implying residence time over about 5 years.
steps.quote: This indicates that the springs are not affected by significant seasonal variations, suggesting that the groundwater residence time may be longer than approximately 5 years

steps.action: Convert the end-member depletion with literature altitude gradients into a recharge altitude (210-840 m) and attribute recharge to Mt. Urabu (231 m).
steps.quote: suggesting that the fresh water is coming from such an altitude

steps.action: Estimate the seawater percentage of each spring from Cl relative to standard seawater (Eq. 1), giving about 3% for YSd and about 5% for the others.
steps.quote: Among the five springs sampled in this study, only YSd had a low seawater percentage of 3%, while the other springs were around 5%

steps.action: Recompute seawater fractions from the 1979 and 1995 data and compare them, noting that the old sample locations are uncertain.
steps.quote: the effect of seawater on the spring water around Sanninudai is clearly stronger than in the past

steps.action: Compare the ranking of seawater fractions with the south-to-north positions of the springs and infer a freshwater source to the north.
steps.quote: the freshwater source is located in the north and the influence of seawater is stronger to the south

steps.action: Estimate a piston-flow recharge year from SF6 using an atmospheric-equilibrium curve set at Mt. Urabu altitude and mean island temperature, after a 5% seawater correction.
steps.quote: Converting this value to the age of the groundwater at atmospheric equilibrium, we obtained a result of ~2016

steps.action: Vary the excess-air assumption up to a five-fold effect (recharge about 1986) and check that the seawater correction changes SF6 only within error.
steps.quote: assuming that the maximum five-fold effect was observed, the observed concentration in this study could be

steps.action: Check the SF6 age against the independent isotope-seasonality indicator and conclude that mean residence time exceeds 5 years.
steps.quote: no seasonal variation was observed, suggesting that the residence time is likely to be more than 5

steps.action: Compare the residence time with SF6 ages published for a similar Ryukyu limestone aquifer on Tarama Island.
steps.quote: fits relatively well with values measured along the coast of the island

steps.action: Plot Ca against HCO3 relative to the 1:2 carbonate-dissolution line and the seawater dilution line; the springs show excess Ca attributed to seawater or sea salt.
steps.quote: may drive the data from springs with high Ca ratios away from the 1:2 line

steps.action: Calculate CaCO3 saturation indices with The Geochemist's Workbench from observed temperature, pH, Ca and alkalinity.
steps.quote: the saturation index (SI) for each sample was calculated

steps.action: Compare saturation states: the springs are supersaturated off the dissolution line, while basin groundwaters are supersaturated but on it (buffered).
steps.quote: while all spring waters are supersaturated for CaCO3

steps.action: Propose that the seawater component, possibly sea-salt particles in surface soils, enters just before discharge rather than through buffered aquifer intrusion.
steps.quote: it is possible that the influence of sea salt particles is limited to surface soils around

steps.action: Build cross-sections from published basement and water-table elevations and refine the flow path from YSd through YSa to YSc, reassigning the springs to the Minami-Ndan basin.
steps.quote: we propose that groundwater is supplied to the second gravel layer containing YSa spring water

steps.action: Retain a conceptual groundwater-flow model for the spring area as the paper's conclusion.
steps.quote: Based on these findings, we constructed a conceptual diagram of groundwater flow in the vicinity of the spring area.

tree.answer: Brackish, limestone-influenced springs at Sanninudai with an unclear source and flow path
No; source, recharge altitude, residence time and mixing are inferred from tracers
Clarify the discharge mechanism and groundwater flow path
Implicit: aquifer seawater intrusion versus sea salt added near the outlet; Barumi versus Minami-Ndan basin as source
Partly; the saturation-index pattern (buffered versus unbuffered) separates aquifer intrusion from near-outlet addition
Conditions found in natural springs, sampled on three dates
Residence time bounded across excess-air assumptions and matched by isotope seasonality; seawater fraction stable across dates
Highland fresh water mixed with about 3-5% seawater near the outlets; outlet of the Minami-Ndan basin

end.claim: The Sanninudai springs discharge fresh water recharged at high elevation (Mt. Urabu) and retained for more than about five years, with about 3-5% seawater or sea salt added near the outlets; they are better described as outlets of the Minami-Ndan basin than of the Barumi basin.

decisive_move.sentence: Estimating the freshwater isotope end-member and the about 5% seawater mixture from the isotope-Cl regressions underlies the high-altitude recharge source, the seawater correction of SF6, and the flow model.

gates.evidence: SF6 and the other analytes were measured to elucidate flow paths, not to test a stated hypothesis (p. 3). The near-outlet seawater interpretation rests on a saturation-index pattern that could have looked otherwise (pp. 12-13). Residence time is cross-checked by two indicators (p. 10). The Minami-Ndan reassignment rests on elevation reasoning from published data with no test (p. 14). Nothing is reported as fixed before the data.

limits:
The XML text supplied contains only the abstract and captions, so body steps cite printed pages. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded.

Sub-claims and their statuses:
- Seawater fraction of 3-5%: estimate_with_resolution, without stated uncertainty.
- Mean residence time over 5 years: estimate_with_resolution, but weakly bounded. The SF6 age spans 1986-2016 depending on an assumed excess-air factor, and the conclusion states both "at least three years" and more than five years.
- Recharge at Mt. Urabu: best_explanation. The altitude calculation gives 210-840 m, mostly above the island's highest peak, and the authors resolve this by assertion.
- Increasing seawater over time: tentative, with no status. It relies on old samples whose locations are unclear.
- Near-outlet sea-salt addition and Minami-Ndan outlet: best_explanation.

Gaps in what the paper shows:
- SF6 was measured only at YSa, so the age applies to one spring.
- No regression statistics are given for the end-member fit.
- Flow rates were not measured in this study.
- Rival explanations are not stated explicitly. The rivals coded are inferred from the text.
- The order of work (whether the flow model preceded or followed data inspection) is not described. This is inference.

disagreements.target: Kurokawa et al. (1979): Sanninudai springs as outlets of the Barumi Groundwater Basin
disagreements.support: Basement and water-table elevations from the same 1979 survey, combined with spring elevations of 10-15 m, place the source in the upstream Minami-Ndan basin.
disagreements.quote: but is more appropriately considered an outlet on the east coast of the Minami-Ndan Groundwater Basin

disagreements.target: Seawater contributions computed from Agata (1995) and Kurokawa et al. (1979) spring data (1.5% and 2.3%)
disagreements.support: Recomputed fractions from the older data are lower than the about 5% found in 2019, read as an increase while noting that sample locations are unclear.
disagreements.quote: the effect of seawater on the spring water around Sanninudai is clearly stronger than in the past
